pages.text: "Wind! Let's fly kites!" Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, flung off their boots. Off went the hat, then the bundle of kite string. Five pegs stood in a row on the wall.
"My kite will fly highest today!" Leo the know-it-all fox took off his collar and hung it on an empty peg. Ppino was already hopping over the doorstep.
Wind whistled outside the lodge. Leo's kite was already in the sky. Ppino stood holding only a kite. "Huh? Where's my kite string?"
Ppino searched all over the lodge floor. Not under the boots, under the long bench, or beside the stove. "I know I left it somewhere here!"
The sun leaned toward the mountain peak. The wind eased, and Leo's kite drifted down. Ppino's kite still lay on the ground.
Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, sat beside Ppino and looked up at the wall. "Shall we hang one thing on each peg?" Three of the five pegs were empty. Ppino had thrown three things too.
Grandma hung up the boots, and Ppino hung up the hat. "One thing on each peg!" Ppino sang along. Now one empty peg remained.
Ppino lifted the bench cushion. Out rolled the bundle of kite string! "Found it!" Ppino's ears leaned forward first. The string went onto the last peg.
The next morning, Ppino sang in front of the five pegs. "One, take it off, hang it up! Two, one thing on each peg! Three, hang everything, then play!" Not one peg was empty.

Outside the lodge, Ppino's kite flew highest. Grandma lifted Ppino into her arms. Put things in their places, and you find them right away. Ppino pointed at the five pegs and called, "One thing on each peg!"
